text.p: Italian debt markets decided to take a rest at the end of a hectic week which saw another round of record highs.
Traders said after a reasonable start and a brief sell-off the market had settled in to a range with little seen to disturb that for now.

The 1997 budget is in the last strait of being approved in the lower house of parliament, with ratification of the last articles likely to be completed by Saturday 1200 GMT. The completion of the budget in the lower house will augment speculation about a nearterm return of the lira to the ERM.
Government ministers have said Italy is likely to request a return to the currency grid by the end of November once the budget was approved in the lower house.
The December future on LIFFE was eight basis points up at 127.54 with support at 127.00, 126.50 and 125.90. Resistance was plotted at 127.60/70 and 128 00.
The July 2006 Btp ended 16 basis points higher at 108.82, with the yield on the 10-year bond at 7.59 percent and the spread over 10-year Bunds 178 basis points.
Traders said they had seen some selling of BTps and buying of gilts in the course of the day.

On the domestic front, the resignation of Public Works Minister Antonio Di Pietro had little effect on the market which did not see the kind of political instability resulting from the move as might have been provoked in past governments.

The focus for next week, apart from the lira and its possible ERM return, is on November preliminary inflation data from 10 cities due on Thursday and Friday. Preliminary forecasts are for a year on year rate of 2.5 to 2.6 percent after October's 3.0 percent.
